The high end has no upper limit, which may be intended but is not stated.

terms.meaning: A number between zero and one showing how well a figure is backed by evidence. The system calculates it and no agent sets it.
A multiplier that makes a range wider. It is at least one.
The working figure that a reader quotes, sitting inside the low and high ends.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and widening formula
sections.what: Explains that weak evidence widens a range rather than removing a process, and describes the formula in words: a factor from one divided by a floor plus a share of confidence, so zero confidence gives four times the width.
sections.why: The docstring says doubtful processes stay in the total, so the reader can see the uncertainty.
sections.watch_out: Confidence must come from the evidence layer, never from a model's own statement.

sections.name: widening_factor
sections.title: Width factor from confidence
sections.what: Turns a confidence between zero and one into a width multiplier between one and four, and refuses any confidence outside that range.
sections.why: The docstring says a value outside that range means the confidence layer is broken, and widening by it would hide the fault.
sections.watch_out: The error stops the run rather than clipping the value, so an upstream bug is noticed.

sections.name: widen
sections.title: Widening a range around its base
sections.what: Widens a range by moving its low and high ends away from the base, leaving the base unchanged. The low end is kept at zero or above.
sections.why: The docstring says the base is widened around, not the midpoint, because the base is the figure a reader quotes.
sections.watch_out: Only the low end has a floor. The high end can grow without limit as confidence falls.

summary: Widens a range of values when the evidence behind it is weak, while keeping the base figure fixed.
purpose: Makes weakly evidenced processes show a wider range of possible value, so they are visibly less certain without being removed from the total.
why: The docstring says removing doubtful processes would make the total look more certain, and that removal would be invisible to the reader.
how: Step 1: take the confidence of the value parameters, which the evidence layer calculates. Step 2: turn it into a width factor, from one for full confidence to four for zero confidence. Step 3: move the low and high ends away from the base by that factor. The base stays where it is.
inputs: A range of values and a confidence number between zero and one.
outputs: A widened range with the same base figure.
risks: A confidence outside zero to one stops the calculation with an error, which protects against a broken evidence layer. The low end is kept at zero or above, but the high end has no cap.
debug: If a range is too wide, check the confidence value for that process. If the widening raises an error, look at the evidence layer that produced the confidence.
